clue.text: Putting money first, directors make cuts here?

indicators.note: putting money first means its word comes at the front, before the directors

parts.note: bread is slang for money
a company's directors sit together as its board

explanation.surface: A company board putting profit first and slashing budgets.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'cuts' look like spending cuts by the directors; really they are slices of a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden board for slicing loaves is where a kitchen knife makes its cuts, a cryptic description.

clue.text: City in need of a plug?

definitions.text: City in need of a plug?

parts.words: City in need of a plug?
parts.note: the English spa city shares its name with a tub that holds water only when its drain is stopped

explanation.surface: A city crying out for publicity, a 'plug'.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a historic spa city in Somerset, England; a bathtub needs a plug to keep the water in.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: the city's name is also a tub that needs its drain stopped before filling.

clue.text: Permit lent it legitimacy in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A permit gave something an air of legitimacy.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit someone is to give them the right, a verb synonym for granting entitlement.

clue.text: Protest fiend with resistance occupying Waterloo maybe

parts.note: a fiend is a demon

indicators.note: occupying means the resistance letter sits inside the word for the London terminus

parts.note: Waterloo is a London railway station, an example signalled by maybe
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A devilish figure leads a resistance sit-in at Waterloo.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo suggests the battle, but here it is the London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration is a public protest, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Predicting vampire hasn't died, or will come round

indicators.note: or will come round means the two letters of 'or' surround the shortened vampire

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: hasn't means the vampire's name is without the letter for died

parts.note: Dracula is the most famous vampire
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A vampire who hasn't died after all may come round again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come round' suggests reviving from a faint; here 'or' literally goes round the shortened vampire.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracular describes prophetic utterance, like an oracle foretelling the future, so it fits predicting as an adjective.

clue.text: Religious leader giving short talk

indicators.note: short says the word for talk loses its final letter

parts.note: rabbit is British slang for talk at length, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork'

explanation.surface: A religious leader giving a brief address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the last letter from RABBIT; to rabbit on is British slang for chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish teacher and spiritual leader of a congregation.

clue.text: Censor's given good report

parts.note: a censor's job is to ban things

explanation.surface: The censor has given a favourable review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' here is a loud noise, as of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A report can be an explosive noise, like a gunshot, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Player in area leaves — about time!

indicators.note: about means the salad leaves go round the time letter

parts.note: cress is a plant grown for its salad leaves

explanation.surface: A player leaves the field, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is the noun, salad greens.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a performer in a play, and a female one is an actress.

clue.text: Plucky player, one thwarting poacher's goals?

parts.note: game means brave or plucky
a keeper is a player, the one guarding the goal

explanation.surface: A brave goalkeeper denies the striker who poaches goals.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a poacher is a striker who scores opportunist goals; here the poacher is a game thief.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate warden protecting game birds stops illegal hunters achieving their aims, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Drink the setter knocked over Pole?

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: knocked over means the word for the setter is turned back

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Polish drinker floored the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' reads as a Polish person; the question mark flags it as a carved column.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved emblem post in Pacific Northwest culture is called a totem pole, so the emblem stands for the column.

clue.text: Men overwhelmed by silent support back in garden

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the soldiers sit inside the reversed words
back means the words for silent and support are read in reverse

parts.note: mute means silent
a bra is a supporting undergarment
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Men drowned out by people silently backing them in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MUTEBRA into ARBETUM, and 'overwhelmed by' places OR within it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a botanical garden devoted to trees.

clue.text: Main criterion changes — there'll be a reprisal

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: If the main criterion shifts, expect retaliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Recrimination is a counter-accusation, retaliating against an accuser, so it is a kind of reprisal.

clue.text: Playful language? Move slowly, that's scary!

parts.note: a tongue is a language
to inch is to move slowly
eek is a cry of fright

explanation.surface: Someone using jokey words creeps forward, then shrieks in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue-in-cheek describes something said ironically or jokingly, not to be taken seriously.

clue.text: Apparent teen slob is working

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A lazy teenager seems to have a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' looks like the teen's employment; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means seeming or professed, a synonym for apparent.

clue.text: Insubstantial odds upset cartel

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds at a race's start

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the cartel are knocked into disorder

explanation.surface: Betting odds overturned by a criminal cartel's interference.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is the bookmakers' odds when a horse race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectral means ghostly, and ghosts are thin, insubstantial things.

clue.text: Paper good at absorbing blows?

definitions.meaning: thin soft paper, as used for wrapping
a paper handkerchief soaks up nose-blowing

explanation.surface: Paper that can take a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows' suggests punches; it is blowing the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin wrapping paper and a paper handkerchief share the same word.

clue.text: Rejects revealed fisherman's actions

parts.note: out means revealed, as a secret is out
an angler casts a line

explanation.surface: Rejected fish are shown up by the angler's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Outcasts are people rejected by society, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Make attractive finale with organ

parts.note: a finale is the end
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A concert finale made appealing by the organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the musical instrument; it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone liked or attractive to others.

clue.text: Storage for artists

definitions.meaning: sliding compartments in a chest for keeping things

explanation.surface: Where artists keep their stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Chest compartments and people who sketch share the same spelling.

clue.text: Ponder alcohol in stewed tea

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic spirit
taken as written

indicators.note: stewed means the tea letters are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: Musing over tea that has been laced with spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is used as it stands, a word of the answer, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to think deeply, a verb synonym of ponder.

clue.text: Forgive a bishop on crack

indicators.note: on means the first pieces come before the word for crack

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to crack a puzzle is to solve it

explanation.surface: A bishop who has turned to drugs seeks forgiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like the drug; it means solve.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to pardon or release from guilt, a verb synonym of forgive.

clue.text: Number-crunchers assist Titanic at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Helping the Titanic out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Statisticians analyse numerical data, so they are literally people who crunch numbers.

clue.text: Rag supports broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is spoken out, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: tees are supports for golf balls

explanation.surface: A newspaper backs a programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rag' suggests a tabloid newspaper; it is the verb meaning mock.
explanation.definitionFit: To rag someone is to mock or taunt them playfully, a verb synonym.

clue.text: If these are taken, it means war

definitions.text: If these are taken, it means war

parts.words: If these are taken, it means war
parts.note: taking up weapons is the idiom for going to fight

explanation.definitionFit: To take up arms is an idiom for starting to fight, so weapons taken signal war.

clue.text: Cook nine basil plants

indicators.note: cook means the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A recipe calling for nine sprigs of basil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a kitchen instruction, and basil a herb, but they are the rearrangement signal and its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Biennials are plants that complete their life cycle in two years.

clue.text: Occasionally indulge then run briefly — lazybones

indicators.note: occasionally picks every other letter of indulge

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A lazy person treats themself now and then, then jogs a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazybones is a person who avoids work, which is exactly an idle person.

clue.text: Stop ignoring cold comfort

indicators.note: ignoring means the cold letter is left out of the word for stop

parts.note: to cease is to stop
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Stop dismissing the cold comfort offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold comfort' reads as a set phrase but splits: cold is the letter removed, comfort the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is relief from pain or worry, a noun synonym of comfort.

clue.text: Chaos destroyed Greens — they might let one know!

parts.note: a mess is chaos

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of greens are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Political turmoil wrecks the Green Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Couriers bearing news are the people who would let someone know something.
